android.desc:
mindLAMP is a clinical and research app developed by the Digital Psychiatry Program at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, a Harvard Medical School–affiliated teaching hospital. If you are part of a LAMP clinical study, you may download the app after completing informed consent with study staff. A standalone companion app is available for Google WearOS devices. If you are not part of a partner study or clinic, you will not be able to access the app.

mindLAMP supports clinicians and researchers by securely collecting health and activity data from study participants. Depending on the study requirements, and only after users provide explicit consent, the app may collect the following data types through Health Connect:

HeartRate, Steps, Speed, TotalCaloriesBurned,  Distance,  Hydration, Nutrition, BloodGlucose, BloodPressure, BodyTemperature, Sleep, RespiratoryRate, and ActiveCaloriesBurned.

These data types are used solely for approved clinical research and patient-care insights as explained during the study’s informed consent process. Users may choose whether to allow or deny data collection, and can continue using non–data-collection features even if they decline.

The app is available in multiple languages: English, Korean, French, Danish, German, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese. Switch to your preferred language for a more personalized experience.

For details on the privacy policy and terms of use, please refer to the handouts provided by study staff.
